summary: Defines a vendor-specific mobility option for Mobile IPv6 Mobility Header messages, so vendors can extend the protocol for research or deployment. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: This makes a slot in Mobile IPv6 messages where each company can put its own private notes, without breaking others.

questions: how to extend mobile ipv6 messages
subtitle: A Mobile IPv6 option that lets vendors attach their own data to Mobility Header messages.

tldr.problem: Mobile IPv6 vendors needed a way to add their own data to Mobility Header messages for research or deployment.
tldr.mechanism: A new mobility option carries a Vendor ID (a Private Enterprise Number), a vendor-defined Sub-type and vendor data. Implementations that do not recognize it skip it.
tldr.outcome: It suits simple extensions only. Complex extensions that modify Mobile IPv6 itself MUST be standardized in the IETF. The option type value is 19.

today: RFC 5094 is a Proposed Standard published in December 2007, and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why a Vendor-Specific Option
sections.content:
Vendor-specific messages let vendors extend protocols and stand apart from each other. They are marked by a Vendor ID, and implementations that do not recognize it discard or skip the message.

RFC 5094 defines the Vendor-Specific Mobility Option for Mobile IPv6 (RFC 3775). It can be carried in any Mobility Header message and MUST be used only with one. Mobility options can be skipped when their type is not recognized. The RFC says the same option can be used for NEMO and Proxy MIPv6, since they also use Mobility Header messages.
sections.eli5: It is like a blank line on a form where each company can write its own note. Companies that cannot read the note just skip it.

sections.title: The Option Format
sections.content:
The option has an alignment requirement of 4n+2. It has five parts: Type (8 bits, marks the option as vendor-specific), Length (8 bits, option length in octets excluding Type and Length), Vendor ID, Sub-type (8 bits) and Data.

The Vendor ID is the SMI Network Management Private Enterprise Code from the IANA-maintained Private Enterprise Numbers registry. The Sub-type says what kind of vendor information follows, and the vendor administers it. The Data is vendor-specific.

If the message also has a Binding Authorization Data option, the Vendor Specific option should appear before it. Multiple Vendor-Specific options MAY be present in one message.
sections.eli5: Each note says which company wrote it, what kind of note it is, and then holds the note itself.

sections.title: Intended Use and Limits
sections.content:
The option is meant for simple cases where adding some vendor data to standard Mobile IPv6 exchanges is enough. It is not suitable for complex extensions that modify Mobile IPv6 itself. Vendor extensions can cause serious interoperability problems and adverse operational impact if not designed and used carefully.

Because RFC 3775 requires unrecognized options to be ignored, extensions using this option should require an indication in the response, also using the vendor-specific option, that the option was processed.

Vendors are encouraged to bring extensions to the IETF. Complex extensions that modify Mobile IPv6 itself, will see large-scale deployment or involve industry consortia or other multi-vendor organizations MUST be standardized in the IETF.
sections.eli5: The private note slot is for small things. Big changes to how the game works have to be agreed by everyone.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: Messages with the Vendor-Specific option should be protected like Binding Updates and Binding Acknowledgements if they carry information that should not be revealed on the wire or that can affect the binding cache entry at the home agent or correspondent node. In particular, messages containing the option MUST be integrity protected.
sections.eli5: Private notes must be sealed so nobody can change them on the way.

sections.title: IANA Assignment
sections.content: The Vendor-Specific mobility option has been assigned the type value 19, allocated from the same space as the Mobility Options registry created by RFC 3775.
sections.eli5: The slot has been given its own number, 19, so everyone can spot it.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: Octets in the option, excluding Type and Length.

fields.name: Vendor ID
fields.desc: SMI Network Management Private Enterprise Code.

fields.name: Sub-Type
fields.desc: Kind of vendor information; administered by the vendor.
